name: NJ-05
label: Safe D

key_factors: Gottheimer's massive financial advantage ($12.8M cash vs. ~$8K)
Incumbency in a district with a modest Democratic lean (D+2)
Prediction markets price Gottheimer at 90-97% to win
Challenger Kirrane has raised only ~$56K with no outside support
model.rationale: Gottheimer is a well-funded two-term incumbent in a district that leans Democratic, and markets price him at 90-97% to win. His challenger's fundraising is negligible, so the race stays safely Democratic despite the modest district lean.
model.watch: Any late surge in Republican outside spending or a polling surprise showing Kirrane within single digits would warrant a downgrade to Likely D.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Josh Gottheimer seeks another term in a northern New Jersey district that leans slightly Democratic. He enters the general election with a huge resource edge, holding roughly $12.8 million on hand after raising $4.8 million, while Republican Sean Kirrane has raised about $56,000 and reports only a few thousand dollars in the bank. No outside groups have invested meaningfully in the race on either side.

Prediction markets strongly favor Gottheimer, pricing his win probability between 90 and 97 percent. No public general-election polls are available, so the outlook rests on the district's partisan lean, the incumbent's financial dominance, and market pricing. The race remains Safe Democratic, with limited evidence pointing to a competitive contest.
